text.p: Reynolds Metals Co said Wednesday progress toward cost-cutting goals continued in the second quarter when conversion costs were reduced $33 million per year, and results from its portfolio review are expected to contribute to earnings this year.
"All this improvement is set against a backdrop of strengthening aluminum industry fundamentals," chief executive Jeremiah Sheehan said.
The company reported second-quarter net income of $55 million, or $0.76 per share. This is compared to 1996 second-quarter net income of $60 million, or $0.81 per share.
The First Call consensus for the latest quarter was $0.72 per share.

This year's profit was after a net charge of $4 million, or $0.05 per share, that included $15 million, or $0.21 per share, for expenses related to personnel reductions, principally at the company's headquarters, which was partially offset by a net gain of $11 million, or $0.16 per share, on the sale of assets in the quarter.
Revenues in the latest period were $1.79 billion compared to $1.83 billion in the second quarter of 1996.
Aluminum shipments of 432,000 metric tonnes were even with the 1996 second quarter, Reynolds said.

In the second quarter, Sheehan said, "Lower prices for fabricated products were offset by progress in our performance improvement program and higher sales volumes in our distribution, wheels, can and packaging businesses."

"We continued to make progress toward our performance improvement goal of $100 million for the year. In the second quarter, we reduced conversion costs by $33 million. We also lowered interest expense," said Sheehan.

"Our portfolio review continues to progress. The review has involved a major restructuring of assets and reorganization of the company as we have moved aggressively to refocus our business for growth into the next century.

"We expect most of the actions resulting from the review to be completed by the end of 1997. Results of the review will begin to contribute to earnings this year and will have a greater impact in 1998," said Sheehan.
